   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

parts of your letter you do not

From: Rudolf Pirsch, GERMANY



Is it possible to bring an
OUTCLASS file (Code 34568,xxxx)
de-compressed to a Tasword file
(Code 32000,xxxx)?

Please excuse my bad English. I
hope you understand what I mean.

       Yours sincerely,

        Rudolf Pirsch

Brian Cavers to Rudolf Pirsch

One or two readers have asked
for this before but I have only
just worked out a fairly simple
way to do it on the Disciple/+D.
I've tried it on a couple of
short articles and it seems O.K.
This is what you do...

1. Load the OUTLET issue which
   has the text you want to
   convert until the CONTENTS
   page appears.

2. Press BREAK.

3. Put THIS issue (60) of OUTLET
   in the drive.

4. Enter MERGE "OPENOUT": RUN

5. Put the OUTLET disc with the
   text back in the drive.

6. Select the article from the
   CONTENTS as usual to load it.

7. Put a blank disc in drive 1.

8. Press A to select "PRINT ALL"

9. Enter a filename. This is for
   the text to be converted to
   an opentype file on the disc.

10.You now need OUTLET 48. There
   is a program called T3TO2
   that will convert the open-
   type file to Tasword 2. Note
   that it will be in 32 columns
   though but you can easily
   reformat it to 64 if needed.

I will put your request to buy a
Disciple in the OUTBOARD message
section.
                        - Brian

P.S. Your English is fine.

From: Dominic Morris, MALVERN


How do you do a POINT (x,y) from
machine code? I tried to use the
line scanner but the machine
crashes. I remember reading of a
routine to calculate the screen
address and bit number from
co-ordinates, but YS forgot to
print the address.

Can you help me?

Thanking you in advance.

Dominic Morris

Brian Cavers to Dominic Morris


To use the Spectrum ROM screen
address routine for either POINT
or PLOT...

LD Y coordinate in Register B

LD X coordinate in Register C

CALL 22AA hex (=8874 dec)

This routine returns with the
screen address of the pixel
coordinate in HL and the pixel
position (as the bit number from
right to left, e.g. 7 to 0) in
Register A.

                      - Brian

From: M.M. Forbes, NEWARK

I am trying to get information
on the Plus D for my son who is,
unfortunately, deaf but who is
more coversant with computers
than I am. He is interested in
word processors, spreadsheet,
database etc. He has managed to
make use of an original version
of Tasword 2 with his Plus D and
disc drive - but tells me there
is a better program called "The
Last Word". Is this true and is
it available anywhere?


Our system is Spectrum 128k
(Grey), Plus D, single drive,
double-sided, 80 track + Star
LC200 Colour printer(via Datel).

Incidentally, the colour driver
software supplied enables
printing of a screen about half
A4 size via Snapshot+Key No.1 or
with SAVE SCREEN$ 1 and the full
A4 size using Snapshot+Key No.2
or with SAVE SCREEN$ 2.

However, without the colour
driver and using the printer as
a black and white set up,
Snapshot+Key2 or SAVE SCREEN$ 2
produces the same large A4 size
printout, but the commands with
Key No.1 DO NOT produce a half
A4 full width printout but only
a small printout on the left
hand side of the paper. Surely
it must be possible to print a
full width 1/2 A4 size picture
in black and white.

Can you or your magazine shed
any light on this please?

I would welcome any help you can
supply and will, of course, pay
the going rate.

Thanks once again.

       Yours sincerely,

        Malcolm Forbes

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Forbes

There have been several word
processors for the Spectrum but
there are few suppliers now and
I don't know of any that has THE
LAST WORD. Your best bet is
probably to scour the classified
adverts in MICROMART or COMPUTER
MART for a second-hand copy.

Another advanced wordprocessor
you might like to consider is
WORDMASTER. This is `13.95 from
P.C.G. 61 School Street, Barrow-
in-Furness, Cumbria, LA14 1EW.
It can also be expanded into a
desktop publishing package with
graphics mixed with the text and
larger text styles by getting
HEADLINER (`10.95) and TYPELINER
(`18.95)or all three for `37.95.

If you order it, please state it
is for the +D as they do various
versions and also say OUTLET
recommended it!

The definitive Spectrum database
is MASTERFILE and this used to
be advertised at `14.95 from
TRANSFORM LTD, 7c Station
Approach, Hayes, Kent, BR2 7EQ.
I recommend you call them first
on 081 462 4666 before sending
any money because I have not
seen them advertise for a while
now. If they can supply MASTER-
FILE you may need to get the
tape version and convert it to
disc. It is fairly simple to
alter the SAVE and LOAD syntax
in the BASIC. You may also need
MF-PRINT (`6.95) to use it with
a large printer.

TRANSFORM also used to sell a
spreadsheet program called
OMNICALC but you had better ask
them about running on +D disc
before ordering!

Another program of interest is
THE PERSONAL BANKING SYSTEM from
HILTON COMPUTER SERVICES, 3
Suffolk Drive, Guildford, Surrey
GU4 7FD for `12. Please state
you want the +D version. I've
not seen this but it is a very
comprehensive calc/database that
is reputed to be good enough to
run a small business as well as
keeping track of your own
personal finances etc. Hilton
are on 0483 578983. As ever, if
you order, please say you heard
of them in OUTLET - it does help
us!

Last, but certainly not least,is
THE BOOKKEEPER for keeping home
or business accounts. This is
only `10 from Francis Miles and
the advert is in our very own
OUTBOARD with more info.

The black and white screen dump
you refer to is the standard
dump being the 256 by 192 dots
of a Spectrum screen printed in
the standard graphic mode of an
Epson-compatible printer. You
need special software to get
different dumps. CHARDUMP in
OUTLET 8 gives a wide dump but
is slow. One versatile screen
dump utility was called DUMPY
but I don't of anyone supplying
it any longer unless you can see
an advert for a second-hand one
somewhere.          - Brian

From: Brian Birkett, CO. DURHAM

Dear Ron & Brian,

I was copying some programs from
OUTLET 51 to a working disk when
by mistake I copied "INDEX DATA"
using Betterbytes 'Organiser'
program with its wildcard
facility. Try as I may, I cannot
ERASE this program even with
Betterbytes 'Organiser' although
it says it has.

It would appear that you use
some jiggery-pokery to put the
program in the catalogue without
any visible parameters. Not
being able to make sense of the
CAT data bytes I wondered...

a) how you did it and...

b) how do I erase the program
from the disc short of doing a
Format?

I gain great pleasure out of
OUTLET and look forward to its
arrival each month.

Thanks for your interest.

        Brian Birkett

Brian Cavers to Brian Birkett

The answer is that on all but
the  PLUS 3 and SAM versions of
OUTLET the word "DATA" in the
filename for the new OUTDEX data
is not the letters D,A,T,A but
the Sinclair keyword token"DATA"
which is CHR$ 228. All the
characters you see on screen
have a code number, for example,
a capital "A" is 65, a SPACE is
32 and the numeral "2" is 50. In
addition, complete keywords such
as "PRINT", "GO TO" are stored
in the computer -not as separate
characters like "P","R","I","N",
"T" but as a single byte, e.g.,
"PRINT" has the code number 245.
This saves space and lets the
computer run BASIC faster.

In 48K BASIC one enters these
keywords in one operation but
even 128K BASIC stores keywords
in this way although you have to
type them in letter by letter.

Years ago I used to use these
keywords a lot in filenames as
it gave a clear indication of a
filetype without using up more
than a single character out of a
precious maximum 10 characters
that one could use in a filename
on all but the +3 Spectrum. For
example...

"galleon SCREEN$" (SCREEN$ FILE)
"pacman CODE"     (CODE FILE)
"draw DATA"       (DATA FILE)

- What could be simpler?!

Then, along comes the Disciple
and +D and, not only is it less
important to show filetypes in
the name because the normal CAT
shows the filetype anyway but
using keywords in the filename
messes up the neatness of the
CAT listing which assumes space
for only 10 characters. In
addition, the Plus 3 is very,
very restrictive in the type of
characters you can use in a file
name and so we decided to adopt
a standard in OUTLET to make it
easier with conversions and when
referring to filenames. The
result was we had to use the
lowest common denominator which
is the Plus 3 and so files now
are generally limited to 8
characters (unless there is a
full stop) and no keywords.

The Plus 3 WILL accept more than
8 characters so long as it is
divided by a full stop and there
are no more than 3 characters
after it.

Anyway, because most readers
already had copies of OUTDEX
which could only load the file
name "INDEX DATA" with the key-
word "DATA" we could not change
it without a lot of hassle so it
stayed as it was.

You can LOAD, SAVE, COPY, ERASE
etc. any filename that contains
keywords by using, e.g.,

      LOAD "NAME"+CHR$ 170

How do you work out the number?
Read on...

You can find the right number by
entering PRINT CODE "KEYWORD" in
48K BASIC where you enter the
keyword you want in quotes by
using the appropriate keys. For
instance, in EXTENDED MODE(Press
SHIFT+SYMBOL or use EXTEND MODE
key) then SYMBOL + "K" to get
the keyword "SCREEN$".To get the
"command" keywords like BORDER,
PRINT and PLOT you enter, e.g.,
"THEN PRINT" and then DELETE the
"THEN". You get the "THEN" in
the first place by using SYMBOL
+ "G".

This may seem complicated to the
beginner but, believe me, it is
as simple as can be and totally
second-nature to us old 48K'ers!

                        - Brian

From: Miles Kinloch, EDINBURGH

Here is a tip for 'RAMMANAGER'.
I discovered if you run this
utility from 128 BASIC the'Quit'
option puts you into the 48K
editor and crashes immediately
if you enter any BASIC command.
(This is because the flag at
23611 is still set for 128K
mode). A couple of of POKEs,
however, will overcome this
problem: once the RAMMANAGER
code is in screen memory, just
POKE 17731,176 and POKE 17732,27
before you use it. When you Quit
afterwards you will be returned
successfully to the mode you had
been using.
            Regards,
                   Miles Kinloch

From: Robert Hunter, FALKIRK


To Ron and Brian,

Regarding "Saving storage space
on +D when using the 'Snapshot'
button",perhaps you already know
about this, but anyway I found
it by trying to make"more room".

1] When you "Snapshot" a program
in memory, it uses 97 sectors or
47Kbytes of storage on the disk.

2] If you re-load this program -
PRESS BREAK,then SAVE D1"SNAP B"
or whatever, - the screen asks
"Overwrite SNAP B?" or whatever,
- PRESS Y. Then CAT 1 and you
will see a saving of 35Kbytes.

This is because the"New"(Snap B)
program is now a BASIC program
using only 27 sectors or
13Kbytes.

3] The only difference I can see
is that when you next LOAD this
program, you have to press "RUN"
to get it to run.

4] The actual steps on a blank
disk were:

  i) FORMAT D1         = 780K
 ii) SAVE DI "+SYSTEM"
      CODE 8192,6656     - 7K
                        -----
                       = 773K
iii) SNAPSHOT PROGRAM   - 48K
                        -----
 iv) CAT 1 free kbytes = 724K

   v) LOAD P2 (re-LOAD)
      "Snapshot" 48k
  vi) Press BREAK
 vii) SAVE D1 "SNAP B"
viii) PRESS Y
  ix) CAT 1  free kbytes =759K

I find myself using my +2 in 48k
mode more now than before I got
my +D.

I always find something of
interest in OUTLET.

       Yours sincerely,

         Robert Hunter.

Brian Cavers to Robert Hunter

Ooops! You've made a slight er..
bloomer! Think through carefully
what you did and ask yourself
the question "why snapshot the
program in the first place?"!!

You see, you have loaded a pro-
gram, snapshotted it, reloaded
the snapshot, used BREAK and
then simply saved it as a BASIC
program which you could have
done in the first place.In other
words, cut out items 3, 4, and 5
in your list. Just load the
original program, BREAK and SAVE
it. Incidentally if you do CAT 1
on the disc with the original
program, the right-hand number
is the AUTO-RUN LINE NUMBER...

If you note down that auto-run
line number (e.g., 10) and then
save the program as...

       SAVE "NAME" LINE 10

It will auto-run each time you
load it.

There is an even easier method
of copying files from one disc
to another. Just use...

       SAVE d1"NAME" to d1

The drive numbers can be changed
if you have more than one drive.

The SNAPSHOT function is only
really intended for commercial
games where BREAK does not work.
                         - Brian

purchased My Plus D Interface
and Drive system from them about
a year ago I was given the offer

system. However, in stating this
I have to say that asking them
for help and information is one
thing, getting a reply from them
is another. Here is the address
to write to if you feel lucky:

DATEL ELECTRONICS LTD, GOVAN
ROAD, FENTON INDUSTRIAL ESTATE,
FENTON, STOKE-ON-TRENT ST4 2RS

Technical/Customer Service
Tel:  0782 744324

With regards to letters about
mail order, I, too, have
experienced great difficulty
with many hardware and software
houses. However, I would like to
recommend a software house that
I have found to be one of the
best around. They are:

BETTERBYTES SOFTWARE, 10 SPITTAL
TERRACE,GOSFORTH, NEWCASTLE-UPON
-TYNE, NE3 1UT

       Tel: (091) 285 6185

I have been in contact with them
for over a year now and the
service that they offer is
second to none. I've had many
software utilities from them
which I could not live without.

The packaging is bubble-wrapped
and the manuals are full and
complete. They offer a full
backup service and guarantee and
the turnaround is very quick
indeed. If you are looking for a
very good software house and
want good value in utility
software then this is the one.
I would state here that I do not
have any part of this company; I
just use their services.

Speaking of BETTERBYTES I've
included a small article about
one of the Software products
called FASTWORD PLUS. If Ron or
Brian have room to publish it.

[I'll feature this as a future
'CHECKOUT' Review -B.C.]

Speaking of software utilities,
and back to Ron & Brian, do you
have any plans to update CAT-
LOADER to run under the Uni-DOS
system? -just a thought!


Still on the subject of Uni-DOS
there was a letter in the June
issue from a reader with regards
to sector error and the MOVE
command in Uni-DOS. I find that
if I get software discs from
outside, (Even OUTLET), I
usually get sector error
messages on most - if not all
other discs from outside. I find
by using the RE-FORMAT utility
on Uni-DOS all the problems and
ERRORS then disappear.

Back to Uni-DOS again:
I wrote in with a query about
whether or not it was possible
to re-align the disc drive head.
Well, I did find a way and no
more problems with the drive.
Inside the Plus D drive the
Read/Write head has two screws
and if gently loosened, (and I
mean GENTLY) the Read/Write head
can be re-positioned and then
the screws tightened again.


I am not recommending this to
other users, I'm just saying
that it worked for me. Also, I
find a setting of 4 (Drive
Stepping Rate) works well under
Uni-DOS and speeds things up no
end.

Lastly, one little tip that
might help many, is that if you
find your Plus D/Disciple inter-
face keeps moving about, and
this is usually when you're in
the middle of a program, the way
to get around this and keep the
interface stable is to use the
Ram Turbo Interface. (They are
quite cheap and useful). Connect
the Ram Turbo Interface first,
then connect the Plus D/Disciple
interface into that. I did this
some months back now and it's
never moved or loosened since.

My thanks again to all who
offered me help and advice; it's
very much appreciated, and to
Ron & Brian keep up the great
work on OUTLET.   - V.L. Jacks

be possible to modify CATLOADER

string array: C$() although at
present the catalogue number (or
"P" number) is stored in the
first two characters of each
element and files loaded with
LOAD Pn. Anyone else got Uni-Dos
and CATLOADER and fancy dabbling
with the BASIC?       - Brian

PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE! Text is accepted in any form for OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files (say which),typed or handwritten letters. However, PLEASE send us a textfile if possible so your letter needn't be typed again! The easiest for us to edit are Tasword 2 files with the right margin set at 32 but a textfile in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be parts of your letter you do not wish published but we always use our discretion anyway. Letters may also be edited for clarity and length... Please ask if you welcome direct correspondence from other OUTLET readers and we will publish your full address.

From: G.L.R. Till, CUMBRIA

Dear Mr. Cavers,

Will you kindly tell me the best way to copy a complete disc on a single drive Plus D?

With regard to Spectrum repairs, I have always been satisfied with: H.S. Computer Services, Unit 2, The Orchard, Warton, PRESTON, Lancs PR4 1BE. Tel:

BETTERBYTES, 10 SPITTAL TERRACE, GOSFORTH, NEWCASTLE-UPON-TYNE, NE3 1UT (TEL: 091 285 6185)

(tell them OUTLET sent you!)

I have not used it myself but BETTERBYTES have a good reput- ation. DISC MATE is advertised as "DISC COPIER & TOOLKIT, MINIMISES DISC SWAPPING" + more! Meanwhile, try SAVE d1"*" TO d1 but this does involve quit a bit of disc-swapping if there are a lot of files!           - Brian

From: Rudolf Pirsch, GERMANY

Is it possible to bring an OUTCLASS file (Code 34568,xxxx) de-compressed to a Tasword file (Code 32000,xxxx)?

Please excuse my bad English. I hope you understand what I mean.

Yours sincerely,

Rudolf Pirsch

Brian Cavers to Rudolf Pirsch

One or two readers have asked for this before but I have only just worked out a fairly simple way to do it on the Disciple/+D. I've tried it on a couple of short articles and it seems O.K. This is what you do...

1. Load the OUTLET issue which has the text you want to convert until the CONTENTS page appears.

2. Press BREAK.

3. Put THIS issue (60) of OUTLET in the drive.

4. Enter MERGE "OPENOUT": RUN

5. Put the OUTLET disc with the text back in the drive.

6. Select the article from the CONTENTS as usual to load it.

7. Put a blank disc in drive 1.

8. Press A to select "PRINT ALL"

9. Enter a filename. This is for the text to be converted to an opentype file on the disc.

10.You now need OUTLET 48. There is a program called T3TO2 that will convert the open- type file to Tasword 2. Note that it will be in 32 columns though but you can easily reformat it to 64 if needed.

I will put your request to buy a Disciple in the OUTBOARD message section.

```text
                        - Brian
```

P.S. Your English is fine.

From: Dominic Morris, MALVERN

How do you do a POINT (x,y) from machine code? I tried to use the line scanner but the machine crashes. I remember reading of a routine to calculate the screen address and bit number from co-ordinates, but YS forgot to print the address.

Can you help me?

Thanking you in advance.

Dominic Morris

Brian Cavers to Dominic Morris

To use the Spectrum ROM screen address routine for either POINT or PLOT...

LD Y coordinate in Register B

LD X coordinate in Register C

CALL 22AA hex (=8874 dec)

This routine returns with the screen address of the pixel coordinate in HL and the pixel position (as the bit number from right to left, e.g. 7 to 0) in Register A.

- Brian

From: M.M. Forbes, NEWARK

I am trying to get information on the Plus D for my son who is, unfortunately, deaf but who is more coversant with computers than I am. He is interested in word processors, spreadsheet, database etc. He has managed to make use of an original version of Tasword 2 with his Plus D and disc drive - but tells me there is a better program called "The Last Word". Is this true and is it available anywhere?

Our system is Spectrum 128k (Grey), Plus D, single drive, double-sided, 80 track + Star LC200 Colour printer(via Datel).

Incidentally, the colour driver software supplied enables printing of a screen about half A4 size via Snapshot+Key No.1 or with SAVE SCREEN$ 1 and the full A4 size using Snapshot+Key No.2 or with SAVE SCREEN$ 2.

However, without the colour driver and using the printer as a black and white set up, Snapshot+Key2 or SAVE SCREEN$ 2 produces the same large A4 size printout, but the commands with Key No.1 DO NOT produce a half A4 full width printout but only a small printout on the left hand side of the paper. Surely it must be possible to print a full width 1/2 A4 size picture in black and white.

Can you or your magazine shed any light on this please?

I would welcome any help you can supply and will, of course, pay the going rate.

Thanks once again.

Yours sincerely,

Malcolm Forbes

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Forbes

There have been several word processors for the Spectrum but there are few suppliers now and I don't know of any that has THE LAST WORD. Your best bet is probably to scour the classified adverts in MICROMART or COMPUTER MART for a second-hand copy.

Another advanced wordprocessor you might like to consider is WORDMASTER. This is `13.95 from P.C.G. 61 School Street, Barrow- in-Furness, Cumbria, LA14 1EW. It can also be expanded into a desktop publishing package with graphics mixed with the text and larger text styles by getting HEADLINER (`10.95) and TYPELINER (`18.95)or all three for `37.95.

If you order it, please state it is for the +D as they do various versions and also say OUTLET recommended it!

The definitive Spectrum database is MASTERFILE and this used to be advertised at `14.95 from TRANSFORM LTD, 7c Station Approach, Hayes, Kent, BR2 7EQ. I recommend you call them first on 081 462 4666 before sending any money because I have not seen them advertise for a while now. If they can supply MASTER- FILE you may need to get the tape version and convert it to disc. It is fairly simple to alter the SAVE and LOAD syntax in the BASIC. You may also need MF-PRINT (`6.95) to use it with a large printer.

TRANSFORM also used to sell a spreadsheet program called OMNICALC but you had better ask them about running on +D disc before ordering!

Another program of interest is THE PERSONAL BANKING SYSTEM from HILTON COMPUTER SERVICES, 3 Suffolk Drive, Guildford, Surrey GU4 7FD for `12. Please state you want the +D version. I've not seen this but it is a very comprehensive calc/database that is reputed to be good enough to run a small business as well as keeping track of your own personal finances etc. Hilton are on 0483 578983. As ever, if you order, please say you heard of them in OUTLET - it does help us!

Last, but certainly not least,is THE BOOKKEEPER for keeping home or business accounts. This is only `10 from Francis Miles and the advert is in our very own OUTBOARD with more info.

The black and white screen dump you refer to is the standard dump being the 256 by 192 dots of a Spectrum screen printed in the standard graphic mode of an Epson-compatible printer. You need special software to get different dumps. CHARDUMP in OUTLET 8 gives a wide dump but is slow. One versatile screen dump utility was called DUMPY but I don't of anyone supplying it any longer unless you can see an advert for a second-hand one somewhere.          - Brian

From: Brian Birkett, CO. DURHAM

Dear Ron & Brian,

I was copying some programs from OUTLET 51 to a working disk when by mistake I copied "INDEX DATA" using Betterbytes 'Organiser' program with its wildcard facility. Try as I may, I cannot ERASE this program even with Betterbytes 'Organiser' although it says it has.

It would appear that you use some jiggery-pokery to put the program in the catalogue without any visible parameters. Not being able to make sense of the CAT data bytes I wondered...

a) how you did it and...

b) how do I erase the program from the disc short of doing a Format?

I gain great pleasure out of OUTLET and look forward to its arrival each month.

Thanks for your interest.

Brian Birkett

Brian Cavers to Brian Birkett

The answer is that on all but the  PLUS 3 and SAM versions of OUTLET the word "DATA" in the filename for the new OUTDEX data is not the letters D,A,T,A but the Sinclair keyword token"DATA" which is CHR$ 228. All the characters you see on screen have a code number, for example, a capital "A" is 65, a SPACE is 32 and the numeral "2" is 50. In addition, complete keywords such as "PRINT", "GO TO" are stored in the computer -not as separate characters like "P","R","I","N", "T" but as a single byte, e.g., "PRINT" has the code number 245. This saves space and lets the computer run BASIC faster.

In 48K BASIC one enters these keywords in one operation but even 128K BASIC stores keywords in this way although you have to type them in letter by letter.

Years ago I used to use these keywords a lot in filenames as it gave a clear indication of a filetype without using up more than a single character out of a precious maximum 10 characters that one could use in a filename on all but the +3 Spectrum. For example...

"galleon SCREEN$" (SCREEN$ FILE) "pacman CODE"     (CODE FILE) "draw DATA"       (DATA FILE)

- What could be simpler?!

Then, along comes the Disciple and +D and, not only is it less important to show filetypes in the name because the normal CAT shows the filetype anyway but using keywords in the filename messes up the neatness of the CAT listing which assumes space for only 10 characters. In addition, the Plus 3 is very, very restrictive in the type of characters you can use in a file name and so we decided to adopt a standard in OUTLET to make it easier with conversions and when referring to filenames. The result was we had to use the lowest common denominator which is the Plus 3 and so files now are generally limited to 8 characters (unless there is a full stop) and no keywords.

The Plus 3 WILL accept more than 8 characters so long as it is divided by a full stop and there are no more than 3 characters after it.

Anyway, because most readers already had copies of OUTDEX which could only load the file name "INDEX DATA" with the key- word "DATA" we could not change it without a lot of hassle so it stayed as it was.

You can LOAD, SAVE, COPY, ERASE etc. any filename that contains keywords by using, e.g.,

LOAD "NAME"+CHR$ 170

How do you work out the number? Read on...

You can find the right number by entering PRINT CODE "KEYWORD" in 48K BASIC where you enter the keyword you want in quotes by using the appropriate keys. For instance, in EXTENDED MODE(Press SHIFT+SYMBOL or use EXTEND MODE key) then SYMBOL + "K" to get the keyword "SCREEN$".To get the "command" keywords like BORDER, PRINT and PLOT you enter, e.g., "THEN PRINT" and then DELETE the "THEN". You get the "THEN" in the first place by using SYMBOL + "G".

This may seem complicated to the beginner but, believe me, it is as simple as can be and totally second-nature to us old 48K'ers!

```text
                        - Brian
```

From: Miles Kinloch, EDINBURGH

Here is a tip for 'RAMMANAGER'. I discovered if you run this utility from 128 BASIC the'Quit' option puts you into the 48K editor and crashes immediately if you enter any BASIC command. (This is because the flag at 23611 is still set for 128K mode). A couple of of POKEs, however, will overcome this problem: once the RAMMANAGER code is in screen memory, just POKE 17731,176 and POKE 17732,27 before you use it. When you Quit afterwards you will be returned successfully to the mode you had been using. Regards, Miles Kinloch

From: Robert Hunter, FALKIRK

To Ron and Brian,

Regarding "Saving storage space on +D when using the 'Snapshot' button",perhaps you already know about this, but anyway I found it by trying to make"more room".

1] When you "Snapshot" a program in memory, it uses 97 sectors or 47Kbytes of storage on the disk.

2] If you re-load this program - PRESS BREAK,then SAVE D1"SNAP B" or whatever, - the screen asks "Overwrite SNAP B?" or whatever, - PRESS Y. Then CAT 1 and you will see a saving of 35Kbytes.

This is because the"New"(Snap B) program is now a BASIC program using only 27 sectors or 13Kbytes.

3] The only difference I can see is that when you next LOAD this program, you have to press "RUN" to get it to run.

4] The actual steps on a blank disk were:

i) FORMAT D1         = 780K ii) SAVE DI "+SYSTEM" CODE 8192,6656     - 7K

```text
                        -----
                       = 773K
```

iii) SNAPSHOT PROGRAM   - 48K

```text
                        -----
```

iv) CAT 1 free kbytes = 724K

v) LOAD P2 (re-LOAD) "Snapshot" 48k vi) Press BREAK vii) SAVE D1 "SNAP B" viii) PRESS Y ix) CAT 1  free kbytes =759K

I find myself using my +2 in 48k mode more now than before I got my +D.

I always find something of interest in OUTLET.

Yours sincerely,

Robert Hunter.

Brian Cavers to Robert Hunter

Ooops! You've made a slight er.. bloomer! Think through carefully what you did and ask yourself the question "why snapshot the program in the first place?"!!

You see, you have loaded a pro- gram, snapshotted it, reloaded the snapshot, used BREAK and then simply saved it as a BASIC program which you could have done in the first place.In other words, cut out items 3, 4, and 5 in your list. Just load the original program, BREAK and SAVE it. Incidentally if you do CAT 1 on the disc with the original program, the right-hand number is the AUTO-RUN LINE NUMBER...

If you note down that auto-run line number (e.g., 10) and then save the program as...

SAVE "NAME" LINE 10

It will auto-run each time you load it.

There is an even easier method of copying files from one disc to another. Just use...

SAVE d1"NAME" to d1

The drive numbers can be changed if you have more than one drive.

The SNAPSHOT function is only really intended for commercial games where BREAK does not work.

```text
                         - Brian
```

From: Vincent L. Jacks, LONDON

Dear Ron & Brian,

First of all my thanks for sending me the OUTLETS that I had missed, namely, April, May, June and July and for all the help and advice that you gave to me. As I've missed so many OUTLETS I've got a lot to catch up on and this is one of the reasons for writing this letter. I would like to pass on some comments with regards to various letters and to pass on my thanks also to some other readers.

My thanks to Mr. Danny Beach of Carmarthen, S.Wales for his kind offer of help and advice with

some of the problems I wrote in about, If you are reading this month's Issue,I will contact you as soon as I can.

Next,thanks go to Mr. Brian Gaff of BG Services for his kind offer of help, also. Again I'm sorry I have not replied to you as yet but I'm way behind with things at home and I will contact you as soon as possible.

I would like to add at this point that the Spectrum family group have got to be the only computer group that will help one another in such a manner.

(Take note other computer users)

Some readers were asking about twin drives and if it's any help the only place I know of is Datel Electronics. When I purchased My Plus D Interface and Drive system from them about a year ago I was given the offer of either a Single or Twin Drive system. However, in stating this I have to say that asking them for help and information is one thing, getting a reply from them is another. Here is the address to write to if you feel lucky:

DATEL ELECTRONICS LTD, GOVAN ROAD, FENTON INDUSTRIAL ESTATE, FENTON, STOKE-ON-TRENT ST4 2RS

Technical/Customer Service Tel:  0782 744324

With regards to letters about mail order, I, too, have experienced great difficulty with many hardware and software houses. However, I would like to recommend a software house that I have found to be one of the best around. They are:

BETTERBYTES SOFTWARE, 10 SPITTAL TERRACE,GOSFORTH, NEWCASTLE-UPON -TYNE, NE3 1UT

```text
       Tel: (091) 285 6185
```

I have been in contact with them for over a year now and the service that they offer is second to none. I've had many software utilities from them which I could not live without.

The packaging is bubble-wrapped and the manuals are full and complete. They offer a full backup service and guarantee and the turnaround is very quick indeed. If you are looking for a very good software house and want good value in utility software then this is the one. I would state here that I do not have any part of this company; I just use their services.

Speaking of BETTERBYTES I've included a small article about one of the Software products called FASTWORD PLUS. If Ron or Brian have room to publish it.

[I'll feature this as a future 'CHECKOUT' Review -B.C.]

Speaking of software utilities, and back to Ron & Brian, do you have any plans to update CAT- LOADER to run under the Uni-DOS system? -just a thought!

Still on the subject of Uni-DOS there was a letter in the June issue from a reader with regards to sector error and the MOVE command in Uni-DOS. I find that if I get software discs from outside, (Even OUTLET), I usually get sector error messages on most - if not all other discs from outside. I find by using the RE-FORMAT utility on Uni-DOS all the problems and ERRORS then disappear.

Back to Uni-DOS again: I wrote in with a query about whether or not it was possible to re-align the disc drive head. Well, I did find a way and no more problems with the drive. Inside the Plus D drive the Read/Write head has two screws and if gently loosened, (and I mean GENTLY) the Read/Write head can be re-positioned and then the screws tightened again.

I am not recommending this to other users, I'm just saying that it worked for me. Also, I find a setting of 4 (Drive Stepping Rate) works well under Uni-DOS and speeds things up no end.

Lastly, one little tip that might help many, is that if you find your Plus D/Disciple inter- face keeps moving about, and this is usually when you're in the middle of a program, the way to get around this and keep the interface stable is to use the Ram Turbo Interface. (They are quite cheap and useful). Connect the Ram Turbo Interface first, then connect the Plus D/Disciple interface into that. I did this some months back now and it's never moved or loosened since.

My thanks again to all who offered me help and advice; it's very much appreciated, and to Ron & Brian keep up the great work on OUTLET.   - V.L. Jacks

Brian Cavers to Vincent Jacks

I did not suggest Datel before because I am not sure that they supply double drives separately from the +D. However, it must be worth a try.

Yes, BETTERBYTES have a good reputation although curiously I can't see their advert in the last few issues of FORMAT.

Where do you get these RAM TURBO interfaces from and how much are they? WHAT are they?! The name seems familiar but I don't know of a supplier off-hand. My +D just crashed while I was typing this funnily enough!

No, we have no plans to produce a Uni-Dos version of CATLOADER. We do not have Uni-Dos because OUTLET needs to be as compatible as possible with everyone else's Disciple and +D. Does Uni-Dos have a "CAT TO STRING VARIABLE" command? That is, is there an easy way from BASIC to load the catalogue into a string variable or string array? If so,it should be possible to modify CATLOADER which stores the filenames in a string array: C$() although at present the catalogue number (or "P" number) is stored in the first two characters of each element and files loaded with LOAD Pn. Anyone else got Uni-Dos and CATLOADER and fancy dabbling with the BASIC?       - Brian

Возможно ли распаковать файл OUTCLASS (Code 34568,xxxx) в файл Tasword (Code 32000,xxxx)?

**Brian Cavers — Rudolf Pirsch**

Пара читателей уже спрашивали об этом раньше, но я только сейчас придумал довольно простой способ сделать это на Disciple/+D. Я опробовал его на паре коротких статей, и все вроде бы в порядке. Вот что нужно сделать...

1. Загрузите выпуск OUTLET с нужным текстом до появления страницы CONTENTS (Содержание).
2. Нажмите BREAK.

Ответ в том, что во всех версиях OUTLET, кроме PLUS 3 и SAM, слово «DATA» в имени файла для новых данных OUTDEX — это не буквы D, A, T, A, а токен ключевого слова Sinclair «DATA», который имеет код CHR$ 228. Все символы, которые вы видите на экране, имеют порядковый номер, например, заглавная «A» — это 65, ПРОБЕЛ — 32, а цифра «2» — 50. Кроме того, полные ключевые слова, такие как «PRINT» или «GO TO», хранятся в компьютере не как отдельные символы, а как один байт, например, «PRINT» имеет код 245. Это экономит место и позволяет компьютеру выполнять BASIC быстрее.

В BASIC 48K вы вводите эти ключевые слова одной операцией, но даже BASIC 128K хранит ключевые слова таким же образом, хотя вводить их приходится буква за буквой.

Много лет назад я часто использовал эти ключевые слова в именах файлов, так как это давало четкое указание на тип файла, не занимая более одного символа из драгоценных 10 символов, доступных для имени файла на всех моделях Spectrum, кроме +3. Например:

```text
"galleon SCREEN$" (SCREEN$ FILE)
"pacman CODE"     (CODE FILE)
"draw DATA"       (DATA FILE)
```

— Что может быть проще?!

Затем появились Disciple и +D, и дело не только в том, что стало менее важным указывать тип файла в имени, поскольку обычный CAT все равно показывает его, но использование ключевых слов в имени файла нарушает аккуратность списка CAT, который предполагает наличие места всего для 10 символов. Кроме того, Plus 3 очень, очень ограничен в типах символов, которые можно использовать в имени файла, поэтому мы решили принять в OUTLET стандарт, чтобы упростить конвертацию и обращение к файлам. Результатом стало использование «наименьшего общего знаменателя», которым является Plus 3, поэтому файлы теперь обычно ограничены 8 символами (если нет точки) и не содержат ключевых слов.

Plus 3 ПРИНИМАЕТ более 8 символов, если они разделены точкой, и после неё не более 3 символов.

В любом случае, поскольку у большинства читателей уже были копии OUTDEX, которые могли загрузить файл с именем «INDEX DATA» только с ключевым словом «DATA», мы не могли изменить это без больших хлопот, поэтому всё осталось как есть.

Вы можете LOAD, SAVE, COPY, ERASE и т. д. любой файл, содержащий ключевые слова, используя, например:

```text
      LOAD "NAME"+CHR$ 170
```

Как вычислить число? Читайте дальше...

Вы можете найти нужное число, введя `PRINT CODE "KEYWORD"` в BASIC 48K, где вы вводите нужное ключевое слово в кавычках, используя соответствующие клавиши. Например, в EXTENDED MODE (нажмите SHIFT+SYMBOL или используйте клавишу EXTEND MODE), затем SYMBOL + "K", чтобы получить ключевое слово "SCREEN$". Чтобы получить командные ключевые слова, такие как BORDER, PRINT и PLOT, введите, например, "THEN PRINT", а затем УДАЛИТЕ "THEN". "THEN" вы получаете в самом начале, используя SYMBOL + "G".

Новичку это может показаться сложным, но, поверьте мне, это проще простого и стало для нас, «старичков» 48K, чем-то привычным!
